aluminum_6061.science: High thermal conductivity (167 W/mK) reduces heat damage but promotes BUE. Magnesium content (1%) can cause staining with high-pH coolants. Requires anti-weld additives and pH 8.5-9.2.

recommendations.reason: Purpose-built anti-stain formula with extreme lubricity. Castrol lab tests show 40% reduction in BUE vs standard coolants.
EP additives prevent chip welding. Studies show 25% better surface finish on 6061.
Crystal-clear synthetic allows visual inspection. Swiss precision formula with balanced pH.
Non-staining chemistry specifically for aluminum alloys.

aluminum_7075.science: Zinc content (5.6%) makes it prone to white staining. Lower thermal conductivity than 6061 (130 W/mK). Aerospace-critical surface integrity required.

recommendations.reason: Vegetable ester base provides exceptional lubricity without staining. Boeing-approved for aerospace aluminum.
Anti-stain technology prevents zinc oxide formation. Maintains T6 temper integrity.
Aerospace-grade formula used by major airframe manufacturers. Chlorine-free.
Swiss precision formula for aerospace components.

steel_1018.science: Low carbon (0.18%) makes it gummy and prone to BUE. Ferrite-dominant microstructure is soft. Need chip breakers and good lubricity.

recommendations.reason: Heavy-duty EP formula breaks chips effectively. Industry standard for mild steel.
Balanced formula prevents BUE while maintaining corrosion protection.
Chlorine-free EP additives provide lubricity without environmental concerns.
Multi-purpose formula with excellent bio-stability for long sump life.

steel_4140.science: Chrome-moly alloy (0.8-1.1% Cr, 0.15-0.25% Mo) with 0.4% carbon. Higher strength requires aggressive cooling. Forms segmented chips at higher speeds.

recommendations.reason: Heavy-duty EP formula designed for alloy steels. Sulfur-phosphorus additives reduce crater wear by 35%.
Proven performance on chrome-moly steels. Excellent heat removal.
Neat oil option for heavy cuts - superior lubricity for interrupted cuts.
Good balance of cooling and lubrication for production environments.

steel_4340.science: Nickel-chrome-moly (1.8% Ni, 0.8% Cr, 0.25% Mo) with 0.4% carbon. Used in aerospace landing gear. Hardness 28-36 HRC requires aggressive EP chemistry.

recommendations.reason: Aerospace-proven on landing gear components. Extreme pressure additives maintain surface integrity.
Heavy-duty formula handles high heat generation. Swiss quality.
Neat oil provides maximum lubricity for difficult alloys.
High-performance synthetic for demanding applications.

stainless_303.science: Sulfur addition (0.15% min) improves machinability but can cause pitting. Thermal conductivity 16 W/mK. Easier than 304 but still requires EP additives.

recommendations.reason: EP additives prevent galling. Sulfur-compatible formula.
Micro-emulsion penetrates chip-tool interface effectively.
High-performance synthetic with excellent cooling capacity.
Synthetic micro-emulsion for demanding applications.

stainless_304.science: 18% Cr, 8% Ni austenitic structure work hardens from 200 to 400 HB during cutting. Low thermal conductivity (16.2 W/mK) causes localized heating. Must maintain sharp tools and avoid dwelling.

recommendations.reason: Maximum EP performance prevents galling. Test data shows 45% longer tool life vs standard coolants.
Extreme pressure additives matched to austenitic stainless. Used by medical device manufacturers.
Vegetable ester provides boundary lubrication that prevents work hardening.
Micro-emulsion for excellent heat removal in low-conductivity material.

stainless_316.science: 2-3% Mo addition for corrosion resistance also increases strength. Even lower thermal conductivity than 304. Critical for medical/marine applications.

recommendations.reason: Medical device industry standard. Maintains surface integrity for implants.
FDA-compatible vegetable base. No chlorine or heavy metals. Used by orthopedic manufacturers.
Heavy-duty EP for demanding cuts. Swiss quality control.
Swiss precision formula for medical components.

stainless_17_4ph.science: Can be heat treated to 44 HRC. Copper precipitates (3-5% Cu) cause abrasive wear. Condition H900 is most difficult. Must not overheat and affect precipitation.

recommendations.reason: Specialized for hardened stainless. Neat oil provides maximum lubricity.
Extreme pressure capability for precipitation-hardened alloys.
Ester-based lubricity prevents overheating that could affect heat treatment.
Neat oil for maximum protection in hardened materials.

titanium_grade2.science: Commercially pure Ti has better machinability than alloys. Thermal conductivity 16.4 W/mK. Still requires careful approach - chips can ignite.

recommendations.reason: Aerospace-proven for titanium. Prevents ignition and galling.
Vegetable ester provides exceptional lubricity. No chlorine reaction risk.

recommendations.reason: Industry gold standard for Ti-6Al-4V. Used by Boeing, Airbus, and major aerostructure suppliers. Test data shows 60% improvement in tool life.
Vegetable ester with extreme boundary lubrication. Pratt & Whitney approved. No chlorine reaction risk.
High-performance synthetic specifically formulated for aerospace titanium.
Advanced micro-emulsion for titanium. Good balance of cooling and lubricity.

inconel_718.science: Nickel superalloy (50-55% Ni, 17-21% Cr, 4.75-5.5% Nb). Maintains strength to 650°C. Gamma double-prime precipitates cause rapid work hardening. Thermal conductivity only 11.4 W/mK. Most difficult common material to machine.

recommendations.reason: Developed specifically for aerospace superalloys. GE Aviation approved. Test data: 75% longer tool life vs standard coolants. The ONLY choice for production Inconel.
